chapters.title: Questions on protecting property and assets
Hazards in the home and roof fencing
Comparing home defense, warehouses, and firearms

summary: Rabbi Soffer discusses the halakhic limits of protecting private property and homes using dangerous security measures, drawing comparisons to a proposed prison defense plan in Israel. He analyzes sources regarding an intruder breaking in, the prohibition against keeping hazards in one's home, and Mishnaic rulings on guard dogs in border towns. The class also considers practical applications involving electric fences, guard dogs, security guards, and home firearm ownership.
subjects: Itamar Ben Gvir prison defense proposal
Masekhet Baba Kamma on guard dogs
Owning guard dogs in Eretz Yisrael border towns
questions: How far is a person permitted by Halakha to go when protecting private property?
What are the rules of ba baMahteret regarding an intruder breaking into a home?
Does Halakha permit keeping trained attack dogs or dangerous hazards in one's home or business?
How does Halakha distinguish between defending financial assets versus defending human life?
